To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the basic representation of the quantum affine algebra of type An(1) can be constructed on a space whose basis is indexed by paths in the lattice ℤ(n +1)ℤ, and that the corresponding q-analogue can also be constructed on the same space.
we have found a new realization of the representation of An(2) on a space of lattice paths and that we have found q-analogues of these results.

the basic representations of An(1), and of its q-deformation, may be realized on a space of (non-periodic) paths in ℤ(ℓ + 1) and ℤ(ℵ0) respectively, where ℓ is a positive integer and ℵ0 is the first transfinite ordinal number.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the representation theory of the Lie algebra An(1) and with the study of a family of solvable lattice statistical mechanical models, the so-called RSOS models, which have the algebra An(1), or its q-analogue, as their symmetry algebra.
the representation theory of the Lie superalgebra sl(1, n) and its q-analogue, and the application to statistical mechanics.
the representation theory of affine Lie algebras and its applications to solvable lattice models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the construction of the basic representation for An(1) presented in this paper is a natural one, and that this is in fact the first time that the basic representation of an An(1) has been realized in such a simple way.
the representation theory of An(1), and the theory of solvable lattice statistical models, have been brought together.

the basic representation of an affine Kac-Moody Lie algebra can be constructed in the same way as the irreducible representations of a semisimple Lie algebra, except that we use paths rather than tableaux and that the construction is not restricted to a fixed level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we give a new realization of the representation theory of An(1), which is a natural generalization of the representation theory for An.
we have constructed the basic representation of a quantum affine algebra on a space of functions of a quantum affine Grassmannian.
a combinatorial problem is solved by a representation theoretic method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a representation of An(2) can be constructed on the space of paths in a lattice of dimension 1.
the basic representation of an affine Lie algebra can be realized as a space of certain paths in a lattice.
the combinatorics of paths in a graph naturally gives rise to a representation of an affine Lie algebra.
